newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's Napocor says power stable despite strike.
newsitem.headline: Manila's Napocor says power stable despite strike.

text.p: The state-run National Power Corp (Napocor) said on Monday power supply on the main island of Luzon will remain stable despite a strike by workers of the Philippine Geothermal Inc (PGI), a unit of Unocal Corp.

PGI operates the fields that generate geothermal steam for the 426-megawatt Makban power plant and the 330-megawatt Tiwi power plant, facilities that supply 17 percent of the total power requirement of the northern Luzon island.
Napocor president Guido A. Delgado said in a statement that the power situation will remain stable throughout the Christmas holidays even if the two power plants had to be shut down.
"Both power complexes are operating normally," said Delgado.
Delgado said that when the strike broke out last Friday, Napocor was able to maintain power reserves at 877 megawatts.
Workers of PGI went on strike after the company launched a downsizing programme. Of the 462 PGI employees, 267 joined the strike, PGI spokesman Edgar Sevilla told Reuters.
The Philippines suffered from daily brownouts of as long as 10 hours in 1993 due to lack of power generation capacity.
